canada.title: St. Paul's nurse wants action on garbage in area near Saskatoon hospital
canada.summary: Saskatoon's fire department prioritizes complaints based on whether they pose a threat to people's lives and safety or whether properties are at risk, leaving concerns like garbage on a list that has reached 1,452 complaints still needing a first assessment.

canada.title: Shooting near Etobicoke community centre leaves 1 male dead: police
canada.summary: One male is a dead after a shooting near an Etobicoke community centre early Tuesday morning, Toronto police say.

canada.title: Residents concerned about Dexter Construction’s Woodville pit expansion
canada.summary: The construction company is seeking to expand its quarry in the Annapolis Valley.

canada.title: Specialized burn treatments deployed for soldiers injured in Alberta military base fire
canada.summary: In Alberta, 21 soldiers remain in hospital, with nine in critical condition, according to a provincial health agency. Fifteen of those patients are on ventilators to help them breathe.

canada.title: Pedestrian struck by vehicle in Brampton suffers critical injuries
canada.summary: A pedestrian is fighting for his life in hospital after he was struck by a vehicle in Brampton on Tuesday morning.

canada.title: Descendants say reviving Japanese Canadian veterans' Legion rights historical wrong
canada.summary: After internment forced its closure, a legion that served Japanese Canadian veterans of the First World War is being resurrected. And as Remembrance Day approaches, members of Royal Canadian Legion - British Columbia Japanese Canadian Branch No. 9 — many of whom are descendants of the Japanese Canadian veterans it served — say joining the long-lost Legion is a way to honour their relatives' memory.

canada.title: More than 250 mm of rain forecast for some B.C. areas as storm makes landfall
canada.summary: The B.C. River Forecast Centre has issued flood watches for the South Coast, Vancouver Island and river basins in the Central Coast and Fraser Valley.

canada.title: From fan parties to game-day tailgates, a guide to Calgary’s Grey Cup festivities
canada.summary: The Montreal Alouettes and the Edmonton Elks will face off at McMahon Stadium on Sunday at 5 p.m. MT, but before that, in typical Calgary fashion, pancake breakfasts, concerts and a rodeo will bring fans from across the country together to celebrate.

canada.title: Zero-till farming has improved Sask. soil. Producers believe more can be done
canada.summary: A recent study found that the move to zero-till farming has increased soil organic matter by 41 percent over the past three decades. Some producers are calling for more action.

canada.title: Dawson City business to offer some primary health care services
canada.summary: Yukon's health minister is calling it a "new model" for delivering some primary health services in the territory — while the Yukon Medical Association questions whether it's the best way to improve care for patients.

canada.title: Ullivik eyes expansion to accommodate Inuit in Montreal for medical travel
canada.summary: Ullivik, a medical lodging facility for Nunavimmiut in Montreal has been too small since the day it opened, according to its director. Now, it could expand to better serve Inuit accessing medical care, but the path forward remains unclear.

canada.title: Public safety-focused budget approved by Fredericton council
canada.summary: Fredericton council approved their budget for 2027, which included lower tax rates for most residents and a focus on public safety.

canada.title: Manitoba volunteers search for unmarked veterans' graves to make sure all get proper headstones
canada.summary: Brandon's George MacKay volunteers with the Last Post Fund, a non-profit that works to add headstones to the graves of veterans buried without one. "You can't just let them be on their own," says MacKay. "They got to be recognized."

canada.title: Federal $1.5B recreation fund barely scratches surface of Winnipeg's aging arena deficit, officials say
canada.summary: A federal plan to spend $1.5 billion on upgrading ice rinks and other recreational facilities across Canada over the next nine years is unlikely to make a big difference in meeting the needs of Winnipeg's aging arenas and community centres, local officials say.

canada.title: Some drug users and advocates say wait times keep people from accessing treatment
canada.summary: Some drug users and advocates say long wait times are keeping people from accessing addiction treatment. The province says it’s aware of gaps in the system and it’s working to address them.

canada.title: These domestic violence shelters can hardly keep up with the cost of groceries
canada.summary: As the cost of living and the price of groceries continue to soar, the people who run domestic violence shelters for women and children are struggling to keep up.

canada.title: N.L. man could be barred from entering U.S. due to Trump Facebook comment
canada.summary: A man in St. John’s, N.L., could be barred from ever travelling south of the border after the U.S. Secret Service flagged a Facebook comment he doesn’t even remember making against President Donald Trump.

bds.h: Rep. Thomas Massie launches bid to impeach U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth
bds.lede: Facing an expected impeachment resolution in Congress, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said he’s eager to litigate the policy choices that he and President Donald Trump have made in Iran and Venezuela.
rows: News conference comes after anti-Trump congressman Thomas Massie pursued impeachment measure against the embattled defense secretary
Hegseth said he's "not worried" about an impeachment effort.

Video. Republican Congressman Thomas Massie is seeking to impeach US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth, accusing him of waging military action against Iran for more than 90 days without congressional authorisation.

GOP Rep. Thomas Massie on Monday introduced new articles of impeachment against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth. CBS News' Taurean Small and Olivia Rinaldi have more on that and all the top news from Washington.
The effort will likely fail, but Representative Thomas Massie wants to push Trump to fire Hegseth before Democrats can launch their own impeachment process next year.
The president said he would stand by Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth if he’s impeached.
